headline: Advance Camping Reservations for Northumberland Shore Access
reservation: Daily vehicle entry is typically managed at the gatehouse, but overnight stays require separate bookings via the New Brunswick Parks system. Seasonal availability for campsites fluctuates, so always verify current operating dates and booking windows on the official provincial portal before arrival.

days.title: Northumberland Strait Coastline

stops.name: Murray Beach Waterfront
stops.detail: Walk the sandy expanse known for warm salt waters and views of the Northumberland Strait.

stops.name: Cape Jourimain Nature Centre
stops.detail: Explore the interpretative trails and view the Confederation Bridge from the nearby observation points.

days.driving: Allow 45 to 60 minutes for coastal transit; conditions vary with wind.
days.note: Tidal shifts can significantly change the available beach area throughout the afternoon.

days.title: Lighthouse and Acadian Heritage

stops.name: Cape Tormentine Lighthouse
stops.detail: View this historic navigation aid which stands as a landmark of the region's maritime history.

stops.name: Aboujagane Woods
stops.detail: Drive inland to witness the transition from coastal dunes to the mixed-wood forests of the interior.

days.driving: Allow 30 to 50 minutes; local roads may be narrow.
days.note: Lighthouse interior access is subject to local preservation society schedules.

days.title: Strait Estuaries and Birding

stops.name: Bayfield Marshes
stops.detail: Observe migratory birds in the wetlands that border the coastal highway.

stops.name: Botsford Parish Coast
stops.detail: Visit small fishing wharves to see the local lobster boats and rural maritime architecture.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local exploration; pace depends on birding stops.
days.note: Wind speeds on the Northumberland Strait can affect walking comfort on exposed piers.

intel.title: Day-Use Logistics
intel.text: The main parking area serves both the beach and picnic sites; verify if overflow lots are active during mid-summer festivals. Spaces near the dunes are limited to protect the sensitive grass ecosystems.

intel.title: Coastal Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular reception is generally stable along Route 955, though it may dip near the low-lying marshlands. Do not rely on digital maps for precise offshore navigation or remote beach access points.

intel.title: Rural Supply Points
intel.text: Fuel is available in nearby Port Elgin or Shediac; the immediate park vicinity has limited commercial services. Ensure tanks are sufficient for returning to the main highway corridors.

intel.title: Tidal Awareness
intel.text: Beach activities are best planned around low tide to maximize the exposed sand bars. Check local tide tables as the Northumberland Strait has unique, often singular daily tidal cycles.

intel.title: Confederation Bridge Proximity
intel.text: Access to Prince Edward Island is via the nearby toll bridge; check for high-wind advisories that may restrict high-sided vehicles. The park serves as a common final stop before crossing the strait.

plan.arrival: Collect supplies in Shediac before heading east on Route 15; check-in for campers occurs at the main gatehouse.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are ideal for the paved coastal roads; check RV length limits for specific seaside campsites.
plan.goldenHour: Murray Beach shoreline offers expansive views for sunset, though colors depend heavily on humidity over the Strait.
